data.title: Accenture Agrees to $25 Million DOJ Settlement Over DEI Hiring Claims
data.description:
Accenture Plc agreed to pay $25 million to resolve US Justice Department allegations that it considered race and sex in hiring and promotion decisions, according to Bloomberg.

The management and technology consulting company was accused of using those factors in employment decisions.

data.title: Abbott to Pay $385 Million to Resolve US Infant Formula Claims
data.description: Abbott Laboratories agreed to pay $385 million to settle US allegations over poor manufacturing practices at two facilities, including one tied to an investigation of a contaminated plant that made powder infant formula, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: STOCKS | India’s Tokenized Corporate-Bond Pilot Moves ₹1,025 Crore in First Three Issuances
data.description:
India’s securities regulator has launched a tokenized corporate-bond pilot that moved ₹1,025 crore through its first three issuances. According to NS3.AI, the pilot links bond settlement with cash settlement while preserving existing legal and economic terms.

SEBI said secondary-market trading and retail participation will be reserved for Stage II.

data.title: STOCKS | Junk Borrowers Line Up at Least $13 Billion in Refinancing Deals
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, global junk-rated borrowers are lining up at least $13 billion in refinancing deals to lock in tighter credit spreads before central banks may raise rates, with Authentic Brands Group launching a $4.2 billion debt refinancing plan on Monday, Mister Car Wash Inc. advancing a $2 billion deal to refinance existing debt and fund shareholder distributions, and TransDigm Group Inc. launching a $2.5 billion refinancing.

data.title: OranjeBTC CEO Gui Gomes to Ring B3 Opening Bell as DIGY11 Begins Trading
data.description: BitcoinTreasuries.NET said OranjeBTC CEO Gui Gomes will ring the opening bell at Brazil's largest stock exchange, B3, tomorrow. According to Odaily, DIGY11 will begin trading on the same day. Michael Saylor said this is the type of expansion STRC was created to support.

data.title: Patrick Witt Says Trump Gave Up 'Historic' Ethics Powers in Digital Asset Market Clarity Act Deal
data.description:
White House crypto adviser Patrick Witt said U.S. President Donald Trump gave up what he called “historic” ethics powers as part of a compromise on the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act. According to NS3.AI, Witt said Republicans had accepted as much as 95% of the requests made by Democratic negotiators.

Witt added that any opposition to the bill in the Senate would now be political rather than substantive.

data.title: Apple Seeks Court Order Requiring OpenAI to Provide Hardware Information
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, Apple urged a federal judge to compel OpenAI to provide information about the AI giant's upcoming hardware products, as Apple accused it of trade secret theft. The judge ordered both sides to try to narrow the scope of their early discovery requests before ruling on Apple's expedited discovery request and postponed the hearing on Apple's preliminary injunction motion to October 14.

data.title: Sagen MI Canada Plans About C$300 Million Bond Sale
data.description: Sagen MI Canada Inc. is seeking to raise about C$300 million ($216 million) through a bond sale as soon as this week, according to Bloomberg. The insurance company is pursuing the offering, people familiar with the matter said.

data.title: CFTC Gives Whistleblowers More Than $150 Million for Enforcement Tips
data.description: The US Commodity Futures Trading Commission said it awarded 10 whistleblowers more than $150 million for information that helped staff bring successful enforcement actions, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Senator Lummis Says Trump Backed Tougher Ethics Rules to Advance Clarity Act
data.description:
Senator Cynthia Lummis said U.S. President Donald Trump agreed to tougher ethics restrictions to help advance the Clarity Act. According to NS3.AI, lawmakers will vote on the bill tomorrow.

The updated draft would give state attorneys general standing to sue over federal officials' conflicts of interest. The bill is intended to divide digital asset oversight among regulators.

data.title: STOCKS | House Democrat Pallone Pushes Back on New AI Special Committee
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, Frank Pallone, the top Democrat on the House Energy and Commerce Committee, said he was concerned that creating an AI special committee would further delay the legislative process.

data.title: Bamboo Insurance Seeks Up to $700 Million in US IPO
data.description:
Bamboo Insurance Services Inc., a home insurance company controlled by CVC Capital Partners, is seeking to raise as much as $700 million in a US initial public offering, according to Bloomberg.

The offering would allow its backers to reduce their stakes.

data.title: STOCKS | U.S. Large Bank Shares Slide on Bank of America CEO Remarks and AI Trade Concerns
data.description:
U.S. large bank shares fell sharply on Monday after Bank of America said trading revenue would be relatively flat compared with the same quarter last year. According to Sina Finance, concern over AI-themed trades also weighed on financial stocks.

Bank of America briefly dropped as much as 5.7% after CEO Brian Moynihan said at the Barclays Global Financial Services Conference that third-quarter trading revenue would be relatively flat year over year. Among the biggest decliners in the KBW Bank Index were Goldman Sachs, down 4.6%; Citigroup, down 3.5%; Morgan Stanley, down 4.1%; Wells Fargo, down 3.0%; Bank of New York Mellon, down 3.5%; and JPMorgan Chase, down 2.2%.

Northern Trust shares briefly fell 4.9% after CFO Dave Fox said the company expected a seasonal decline in results this quarter. Other companies scheduled to attend the Barclays conference include Synchrony Financial, Bank of New York Mellon, Citizens Financial Group, Blue Owl Capital, MSCI, Bank of Nova Scotia, S&P Global, Nasdaq, PNC Financial Services, Equifax, KeyCorp, Apollo Global Management, and Citigroup.

data.title: SLB Seen Benefiting From Higher Oil Production Investment
data.description: According to CNBC, energy trader John Arnold said the underlying supply backdrop for oil was already bullish, while the article argued that refiners are the biggest beneficiaries of the current disruption because crack spreads, or refining margins, have never been wider. It said refiners could continue to post record profits for several years, though their share prices are already at record highs, and noted that oil service companies have rallied but are not yet at all-time highs. The piece said SLB is the largest of those oil service companies and that longer-dated long calls financed by shorter-dated short strangles are the preferred trade.

data.title: Alphabet Shows Signs Of Stabilization After May Correction
data.description: According to CNBC, Alphabet (GOOGL) has been in a corrective phase since May but is starting to stabilize as oversold conditions ease. Fairlead Strategies' Katie Stockton and Will Tamplin said the stock has rallied after a counter-trend buy signal from the DeMARK Indicators on Thursday, reclaiming support near its 200-day moving average around $337. They said the daily chart has improved, with stochastics turning higher and the MACD flashing a buy signal, while initial resistance is near $376 and final resistance is near $402. The analysts said a decisive break below the 200-day moving average would be a long-term setback, while the stock remains in a secular uptrend above its rising monthly cloud model.

data.title: VIX Jumps to 18 as Traders Favor AI Risk Over Fed Volatility
data.description:
According to CNBC, the Cboe VIX Index jumped to 18 on Monday, and options trading on the gauge rose to more than double the 30-day average volume as semiconductors and data-center stocks weighed on the S&P 500. By midday, three of the top five VIX contracts to buy were calls, and the biggest trade of the day was someone buying at least $3.6 million of 31-strike calls expiring in mid-November.

The move came after the VIX erased two days of gains on Friday even as inflation data pushed the odds of a Federal Reserve rate hike at this week's meeting to 90%. By Friday's close, options on the S&P 500 were pricing a 0.8% swing into weekly contracts expiring Sep. 18, below the 50th percentile of volatility expected for weeks with an FOMC meeting, according to analysis from New York-based options manager Carrick Lane. John Marshall, principal at Carrick Lane, said the market appears more comfortable with higher rates and is focusing more on AI than on interest-rate risk. He said equity investors seem to think the FOMC decision is already set and are treating AI as a more immediate concern.

The Merrill Lynch Option Volatility Estimate (MOVE) Index, which tracks volatility in U.S. Treasuries, rose 10 points last week to a 92nd percentile high, according to a note from Cboe head of derivatives market intelligence Mandy Xu. Marshall's analysis also showed volatility pricing for rate-sensitive assets such as the iShares 7-10 Year Treasury Bond ETF (IEF) and the Vanguard Real Estate Index Fund ETF (VNQ) in the upper 90th and 80th percentiles. Even so, those bond-market signals have not been driving stock volatility, and odds of a hike on Wednesday's meeting rose above 91% by midday as equity prices firmed.

data.title: BitFuFu Produces 174 BTC in August, Up More Than 55% From July
data.description:
BitFuFu produced 174 BTC in August, marking an increase of more than 55% from July. According to NS3.AI, CleanSpark's production rose around 1% to 593 BTC, while Canaan's production fell roughly 4% to 44 BTC.

Canaan also sold 3,952 ETH and 54 BTC during the month. The figures highlight mixed monthly production trends among the miners.
